move: tile Y-swings in, X draws, wires connect artboards, swings out
how: A dark magenta stage with perspective:1200px; a 300px XD-purple tile turns in from rotationY:-95/x:-80/opacity:0 (expo.out) over the first 25%. Inside, the two diagonal strokes of the 'X' draw with DrawSVG: the first 0 to 100% at 14%, the second from its far end ('100% 100%' to '0% 100%') at 17%, then the 'd' slides in from x:60 (expo.out) at 24%. Two wireframe artboards scale in from 0.6 with back.out(1.8) (stagger 0.15) at 30%, a start node pops with back.out(3), a dashed wire draws from the left artboard into the tile (power2.inOut) at 40% and a second wire from the tile to the right artboard at 54%, ending with a second node pop. Meanwhile the tile eases to rotationY:14/rotationX:-6 on sine.inOut over 35-75%. Exit at 81%: wires retract to their ends, nodes and artboards shrink and fade, the tile swings out to rotationY:95/x:80.
adapt: Change the tile letters/strokes and colours (#470137, #ff61f6), the artboard positions and the two wire paths (which must start and end at the artboards); keep the rotationY swing-in/out and the sequential wire draws.
port: mount(el, shot) inserts artboards, the full-frame wire SVG and the tile inside el (el needs perspective); animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with swing-in 0-0.25, wires 0.4-0.68, exit 0.81 of D. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; wire coordinates are in a 1280x720 viewBox and must be recomputed if el is a different size.
caveats: wire SVG uses a fixed 1280x720 viewBox with hard-coded artboard coordinates
relies on parent perspective for the Y rotation
stylised Xd tile, not the official Adobe mark
